question: Can a cross-validation-tuned gradient-boosting model predict student achievement from background and study-process predictors more accurately than a standard linear regression?
method: UCI Student Performance (id 320); target G3, G1/G2 dropped; one fixed 75/25 split; tuning by 5-fold CV on train only; baseline one-hot+standardized OLS vs. randomized-search-tuned LightGBM; metric test RMSE.
baseline: Ordinary linear regression on one-hot encoded + standardized predictors (all predictors, G1/G2 excluded).
improved: LightGBM regressor on the same preprocessed features, tuned by 20-iteration randomized 5-fold CV search on the training set; mean over seeds 42-44.
notes: Stand-in dataset, not ICILS 2023; the baseline is a generic linear model, not the paper's method. Single small split (test set of modest size) so differences may be within noise; seed std for LightGBM reflects model/CV randomness only, not split variability. OLS is deterministic (std 0).
